dv-render-butterfly.$description: The BUTTERFLY TYPE PARTIAL for dv-render — butterfly-h (mirrored horizontal wings either side of a shared centre gutter) and butterfly-v (mirrored columns above and below one shared baseline), registered #260 as the s259-D1 fast follower. ONE partial for BOTH orientations, on dv-render-bar's argument: the two share the symmetric domain, the pair validation, the DV-D09 fill rule, the mark writer and the wing arithmetic, and only the axis assignment differs — writing them twice is how the two copies drift. The DOMAIN is symmetric ([-M, +M] over the largest magnitude in either wing), which is what makes both wings share ONE scale; the mirror is the SECOND SERIES, not a sign, so a negative inside a wing THROWS, named, and so does a third series. ⛔ It DISCARDS the core's cartesian furniture (`ctx.out.length = 0`, the dv-render-donut move): both reference implementations draw no gridlines and no value-axis ticks by ds-020 declaration, and on a symmetric domain a tick would read "-40" under a wing whose value is 40 — a misstatement, not merely a redundancy. See knowledge/_tmp/260/butterfly.core-requests.md. Enacts dv-004 (the two butterfly-v wings MEET at the baseline — the pre-engine bake had 0.0px there and the engine cuts half a GAP off each wing, driven at 2.200px in 8 of 8 theme x mode combinations), s116-D1 (24px thickness floor where the band can pay for it), DV-D09 (the two wings bind data/series/1 and data/series/3, the pair both #token-manifests already declare) and DV-D02 (every x is data-fx / data-fw, INCLUDING the centre gutter, which is a FRACTION of the plot — 0.196, the reference's own 90/460 — precisely so the fit can re-derive it). §04.3 on-chart letter keys are deliberately OMITTED: direction is already the non-colour channel, receipted as a delta from the bar contract since #95. requires `data-dv-type="` — the figure must say which butterfly it is; the engine reads the type off the spec, the gate reads it off the figure, and a disagreement between them is the defect this catches.
